item.text: {"classifications":[{"segment_id":"1","code":2,"rationale":"Executive departments and agencies retain discretion whether to require a project labor agreement, but any agreement reached under the memorandum must later bind contractors through specified solicitation and contract clauses and contain prescribed labor terms; those legally consequential contractual results arise through subsequent agency contracting.","evidence":"shall bind all contractors and subcontractors on the construction project through the inclusion of appropriate clauses in all relevant solicitation provisions and contract documents"},{"segment_id":"2","code":2,"rationale":"For any project labor agreement used under the memorandum, the segment mandates prescribed agreement content and legal compliance, which agencies must implement later through procurement and contracting; the accompanying limitations do not alter that dictated contractual outcome.","evidence":"shall provide other mechanisms for labormanagement cooperation on matters of mutual interest and concern"},{"segment_id":"3","code":1,"rationale":"Agency heads must establish internal written procedures and criteria, in consultation with the Federal Acquisition Regulatory Council, within 120 days; the segment organizes future discretionary procurement administration rather than itself dictating a particular contract or legal-rights outcome.","evidence":"shall establish, within 120 days of the date of this memorandum, appropriate written procedures and criteria"}]}
